title:
FUNCTIONS AND GRAPHS,
(SKETCHING QUADRATIC, CUBIC AND RECIPROCAL GRAPHS)
objective: LO: I can sketch quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs from their equations.

content.text: A quadratic graph has the form y = ax² + bx + c and is a U-shape (parabola). A cubic has the form y = ax³ and has an S-shaped curve.
A reciprocal graph has the form y = a/x and has two separate curves (hyperbola) that never touch the axes.

examples.desc: reciprocal, two curves in opposite quadrants

examples.expr: y = x² is a straight line

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: To sketch a graph, find key points (intercepts, turning points) and know the general shape from the highest power of x.
key_idea.caption: The highest power tells you the shape

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – quadratic graph
modelled_examples.question: Sketch y = x² − 4
steps: Find x-intercepts: x² − 4 = 0, so x = 2 or x = −2
Minimum point at (0, −4); U-shape opening upwards
modelled_examples.answer: U-shaped parabola crossing x-axis at (−2, 0) and (2, 0), vertex at (0, −4)
modelled_examples.explanation: Plot the intercepts and vertex, then draw a smooth curve.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – negative quadratic
modelled_examples.question: Sketch y = −x² + 9
modelled_examples.answer: Inverted parabola with maximum at (0, 9), crossing x-axis at (−3, 0) and (3, 0)
modelled_examples.explanation: Negative coefficient of x² means the parabola opens downwards.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – cubic graph
modelled_examples.question: Sketch y = x³ − x
steps: S-shaped curve passing through all three roots
modelled_examples.answer: S-shaped cubic crossing x-axis at −1, 0, and 1
modelled_examples.explanation: Factorising a cubic helps find the roots for sketching.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – reciprocal graph
modelled_examples.question: Sketch y = 3/x
steps: When x = 1, y = 3; when x = 3, y = 1; when x = −1, y = −3
As x → 0, y → ∞; as x → ∞, y → 0
Two curves: one in quadrant 1 and one in quadrant 3
modelled_examples.answer: Hyperbola with curves in quadrants 1 and 3, asymptotes along both axes
modelled_examples.explanation: The axes are asymptotes; the graph never touches or crosses them.

practice.heading: Identifying graph types
practice.instruction: State whether each equation gives a quadratic, cubic or reciprocal graph.

practice.heading: Finding intercepts
practice.instruction: Find the y-intercept and x-intercepts for each quadratic.

practice.heading: Cubic graphs
practice.instruction: Find the x-intercepts of each cubic by factorising.

practice.heading: Reciprocal values
practice.instruction: For y = 6/x, find y for each value of x.

practice.heading: Mixed sketching
practice.instruction: Describe the key features of each graph.

items.statement: y = x² produces a U-shaped parabola
A cubic graph can cross the x-axis up to 3 times
The reciprocal graph y = a/x has asymptotes at x = 0 and y = 0

problems.text: A ball is thrown upwards. Its height h metres after t seconds is given by h = 20t − 5t². Sketch the graph. What is the maximum height and when does the ball land?
The time T hours to travel 120 miles at speed v mph is given by T = 120/v. Sketch the graph for v from 20 to 120. How does doubling the speed affect the journey time?
